facts.fact: The FY2026/27 policy statement for Vote 137 reports civil registration as a service of the National Identification and Registration Authority itself: 123,526 births and 9,935 deaths registered and 150,038 birth and 16,714 death notifications recorded in FY2025/26 to 31 December 2025; it names no civil registration software.

NIRA's FY2026/27 budget estimate is UGX 155.948 billion, all Government of Uganda with external financing of zero and off-budget support given as N/A, and it carries a key service area for civil registration services at district level; the same statement lists insufficient funding for complete civil registration coverage as a vote challenge, and UNICEF funded 392 registration assistants in 160 health facilities from 1 December 2025 to 13 February 2026 (dated to the document's publication year).

NIRA reports that its Strategic Plan III for FY2025/26 to FY2029/30 was finalised in FY2025/26 with all approvals and a National Planning Authority certificate of compliance; the statement does not say whether the plan names a civil registration system, and lists expansion of online registration services among its plans.

systems.tiers: central system; 5,665 biometric registration kits deployed; connectivity for all 122 registration centres for data transmission

systems.country_label: data sharing platform (systems integrated with the National Identification Register)

note: No coverage fact: the statement counts births and deaths registered and gives 80% of districts, municipalities and cities registering vital events (2023/24 base, target 100%) but never says whether registration is digital or on paper. The three governance facts are about the civil registration service, which the document does not tie to a named system.
